units.name: Panel shell and tabs
units.verdict: macOS desktop app, pointer and keyboard. Reviewed at 900x560 (compact height), 1360x860 and 1728x1084, in light, plus dark at 1360x860. Evidence was 15 still captures and code excerpts; the app was not run, so nothing was used with real input and no control was actually pressed. First impression: the panel reads calm and organised, with a clear header, one column and quiet chrome. But the emphasis is in the wrong place on the Timeline tab. The eye lands on the title and then on three empty future stops before reaching the Now card, which is the thing the owner opened the panel to see. Counts: 0 Catastrophe, 4 Major, 13 Minor, 2 Cosmetic. The top problem is the footer tab row: Timeline disappears when it is the active tab, so every tab jumps about 72 CSS px sideways on the first click, and the pointer ends up on a different tab. The selected state is also only a text colour, the same as hover, so two tabs look selected at once (R1, R2). Close behind is the Timeline order, which spends about 180px, half the body at 900x560, on stops with no data before showing the current state (R3). R4 (keyboard) is the only Major rated Likely rather than Confirmed.

units.name: Panel popovers
units.verdict: macOS desktop app, pointer and keyboard. I reviewed one size only, 1360x860 (expanded, light and dark), from 9 captures plus code excerpts; I could not run the app, so nothing here was tested with real input. I did not run the blur audit. By eye, each overlay reads as organised, quiet and correctly above the work, and text contrast passes in both themes. The problems are in how these overlays behave, not how they look. Counts: 0 Catastrophe, 2 Major, 11 Minor, 1 Cosmetic. The top problem is the keyboard. Menu items, attachment rows and reviewer names have no keyboard route, and Esc only closes the reviewer popover, so with the terminal menu or Attached dropdown open it appears to skip them and close the whole panel. The three overlays also dismiss in three different ways, and Attached is the weakest: it stays open when you move to another task.

units.name: Banners and answering
units.verdict: macOS desktop app (pointer and keyboard), the right task panel's banner in every scoped state. Reviewed from 15 captures (light at 1360x860 for all ten states, dark for three, 900x560 for two) plus the code excerpts. The app itself couldn't be driven, so behaviour comes from code and nothing was used with real input. Contrast was computed from theme.rs. First impression: the banner is the clear focal point of the panel in every state. A tinted full-bleed band at the top separates each state well, and the panel reads as organised, except in the PR state, where the banner and the timeline compete. The weakness is what each banner offers. Several states don't give the owner the one thing that moves the task on: the open-ended question sends them elsewhere through a quiet link, may-be-stuck has no action, Looks finished recommends the wrong action, and the lost forms don't say what happened or when. Counts: 0 catastrophes, 6 major, 5 minor, 2 cosmetic. Top problem: the open-ended question, the core of flow 1, can't be answered from its own banner, and its only action is a low-emphasis link that does one of three different things under the same label.

units.name: PR steps
units.verdict: macOS desktop app, pointer and keyboard. I reviewed the PR part of the right task panel from 16 captures (11 states in light at 1360x860, 2 in dark, 2 at 900x560, 1 at 1728x1084) and the Rust excerpts. The app itself could not be driven. Blurred, the panel reads as organised at the timeline level: clear stops and a clean step row. Inside Checks and review it gets busy, because orange marks several different things and no action stands out as the next one. Counts: 0 Catastrophe, 6 Major, 4 Minor, 2 Cosmetic. The top problem is that the panel doesn't reliably answer "what is waiting on whom, and what do I do now?". Orange means both "needs you" and "someone else is on it". The next action is a small link with the same weight as Merge now. With merge steps, the step row runs off the panel at every window size, because the panel stays about 480px wide.

units.name: Human box
units.verdict: macOS desktop, pointer and keyboard. Reviewed the Human box from 8 captures (to-do, waiting and done in light and dark at 1360x860; to-do in light at 900x560 and 1728x1084) plus the code excerpts. The app itself wasn't run, so no control was used with real input, and contrast was computed from theme.rs tokens rather than measured on pixels. First impression: the panel reads as organised. There is one warm box, one blue Done and a clear title, and the finished state is calm. But in the to-do state a second peach band sits on top of the box and competes with it, and the waiting state looks identical to a task you can act on. Counts: 0 catastrophe, 5 major, 5 minor, 2 cosmetic. Top problem: the first line of a human task says "It's waiting for you in Midna.", which sends the owner to a terminal the task doesn't have, when the work is in the box right below. The note field is close behind: it is blank and unnamed, yet the steps depend on it and Done sends it to the waiting agents, with no way back.

units.name: Finish and Note modals
units.verdict: macOS desktop app, pointer and keyboard, compact-to-large window. Reviewed the Finish confirm (Mark done, Cancel, Merge now) and the Note for testers dialog from 10 captures of the real app (1360x860 in light and dark; Mark done also at 900x560 and 1728x1084) plus the code. Busy, failed and already-finished states were not captured, so they were judged from code alone. No browser page exists for this native app, so nothing was driven with real input; the browser was used only to compute contrast. First impression: the dialogs are calm and well organised, with one heading, one line of identity and one action, and the board drops back cleanly behind the scrim. The trouble is in what they leave out and how they behave. Counts: 0 Catastrophe, 4 Major, 3 Minor, 2 Cosmetic. Top problem: closing or pressing Esc while Merging… looks like backing out, but the override merge still goes ahead, and its result is then dropped with no toast, no refresh and no error. Merge now also never says what it overrides.

findings.title: The tab row shifts under the pointer when you leave Timeline
findings.element: Task panel › footer tab row, all sizes, both themes, moving from Timeline to any tab and back
findings.problem: The Timeline tab is left out while Timeline is showing, so the row has three items on Timeline and four everywhere else. Clicking What to do moves that label right by about 72 CSS px (x 1043 to 1126 in the 1568px-wide images timeline-working__light__1360x860.png and what-to-do__light__1360x860.png), and Timeline now sits under the pointer. A second click, or the next tab you meant to reach, lands on the wrong tab. The captures show this: the pointer is left on Timeline in what-to-do, on What to do in context, and on Context in full-log. Tabs also never hold a fixed position, so muscle memory doesn't build for something the owner does all day.
findings.principle: Same thing, same place: navigation keeps a stable position and order [NNG-H4] [NNG-FITTS]. Cause: view.rs:892-894 skips Timeline when it is the active tab.
findings.fix: Delete the `continue` branch at view.rs:892-894 so all four tabs always draw in the same order and position, with Timeline marked selected by the R2 treatment. This adds one 22px-gapped label to the Timeline row, and four tabs already fit at 480px.

findings.title: The selected tab is marked by text colour alone, and hover looks identical
findings.element: Task panel › footer tab row: what-to-do__light__1360x860.png, context__light__1360x860.png, full-log__light__1360x860.png, full-log__dark__1360x860.png, timeline-working captures
findings.problem: Zoomed in, the active tab differs from the others only by a darker text colour, with no underline, fill or weight change. Hover uses the same dark colour, so after any click two tabs look selected (Context and Full log in full-log__light__1360x860.png), and you can't tell which tab you are on without reading the body. On Timeline no tab is marked at all. The selected and unselected colours differ by only 2.98:1 in light (#1c2129 vs #5f6b7a) and 1.91:1 in dark (#e6e9ee vs #a1abb8). The same panel marks its selected log filter with a heavy inverted pill, so one panel has two unrelated selected styles, and the weaker one is on the more important control.
findings.principle: Current location is always visible [NNG-H1]; colour is not the only signal, and a colour-only cue needs 3:1 against its neighbours [WCAG 1.4.1]; one look per role [SEC-4].
findings.fix: Give Look::Foot { on: true } a 2px t.accent bar on the tab's top edge, sitting on the footer's border, plus semibold text, the same idea as `tab_btn` at task_panel.rs:2298. Make hover on an unselected tab t.text_2 (#3d4652) with no bar, so hover can never read as selected. Quieten the log's selected chip to t.accent_soft with t.accent_fg text so the tab stays the stronger signal.

findings.title: Empty future stops come before what the task is doing now
findings.element: Task panel › Timeline › Pending merge, Checks and review, Pull request, then the Now node; no-PR task, all sizes, worst at 900x560
findings.problem: The primary task is to open a task and see what it needs, but the panel leads with three stops that hold no data, including a Checks, You, Review stepper of empty rings. In timeline-working__light__1360x860.png they take about 180 CSS px between the header and the Now card; at 900x560 that is about half of the 368px body. With a long title at 900x560 (long-text__light__900x560.png) the Now card shows only its pill and two lines, and Started is out of view. The code comment at view.rs:1094-1095 says the stop it's at reads first, which the layout doesn't do. The rows are also the kind of label with no data the owner's rule rules out, and the main line reads bottom to top while the stepper inside it reads left to right.
findings.principle: The work dominates and the primary content draws the eye first [SCR-1] [SCR-2]; every element earns its place [SCR-5] [NNG-H8]; owner's rule: no filler labels that show no data. Source: no_pr_nodes at view.rs:2425-2429.
findings.fix: For a task with no PR, replace the three nodes at view.rs:2427-2429 with one quiet row above Now, about 28px tall, in 13px t.muted: `Next: Pull request › Checks › You › Review › Merge`. Keep the full nodes once a PR exists, where they carry data. That puts the Now card about 150px higher and removes the empty stepper. Keep any `stack_on` line and author-review step as a second line of that row when present.

findings.title: No keyboard route to tabs, close, Started or log filters is visible in the code
findings.element: Task panel › footer tabs, close, Started row, log filters; all sizes
findings.problem: The brief includes moving between tabs by keyboard, but no focus handling for these controls appears in anything supplied. `tab_btn` (task_panel.rs:2288-2306) and kit.rs's buttons are divs with an id, a pointer cursor and a hover style. Across all supplied code the only focus handling is on text fields, there is no track_focus or tab_index, and `on_key` (task_panel.rs:2182-2199) only handles Enter in fields. No capture shows a focus ring. The code that draws `c.btn` wasn't supplied, so focus could be added there, which is why this is Likely. If it isn't, the owner must reach for the pointer to change tab, and a panel opened from search can't be worked by keyboard.
findings.principle: Every function works from the keyboard [WCAG 2.1.1]; focus is visible [WCAG 2.4.7]; arrows move within groups, which take one tab stop [MS-KBD]; shortcuts for frequent users [NNG-H7].
findings.fix: Check the `c.btn` draw path first. If it has no focus, give the panel controls a FocusHandle with track_focus and a tab_index, plus a 2px t.accent focus ring. Make the tab row one tab stop with Left and Right moving between tabs, and add Cmd+1 to Cmd+4 for the four tabs, shown in each tab's tooltip. Make the Started row toggle on Space and Enter.

findings.title: Overlay items can't be reached from the keyboard
findings.element: Task panel › terminal menu items, Attached dropdown rows and hover cards, reviewer names, at all sizes and in both themes
findings.problem: Close terminal, every attachment row and every reviewer name are plain divs with on_click and no focus handle or tab stop (task_panel.rs:1807, 1818, 1533-1559, 1944-1967). With the keyboard alone you can't close a terminal, open an attachment or open a reviewer's popover. A hover card's summary, folder, link, Added row and Copy are pointer-only too (task_panel.rs:1544, 2686). No excerpt anywhere uses track_focus or tab_index. The renderer for the Attached chip and the ⋯ button isn't in the excerpts, so those two are unknown.
findings.principle: Every function works from the keyboard, and arrows move within menus and lists [WCAG 2.1.1] [MS-KBD]; hover is never the only path [desktop:HIG-POINTER]
findings.fix: Give c_menu_item, c_drop_item and c_rev_name a FocusHandle and tab stop, with Enter or Space running the same act. On open, move focus to the first item; Up and Down move between items; on close, return focus to the opener. Show the hover card when a row takes focus, with a key for Copy link (Cmd+C on the focused row).

findings.title: Esc closes the reviewer popover but not the other two overlays
findings.element: Task panel › terminal menu and Attached dropdown, while open
findings.problem: escape() clears only rev_pop (task_panel.rs:783-789), and c_term_menu has no key handling (task_panel.rs:1773-1797). Its doc comment says Esc reaches the panel next (task_panel.rs:782), so Esc with either overlay open should close the whole task panel and leave the overlay's flag set. That last step is inferred: the caller of escape() and the K::Drop renderer aren't in the excerpts. Since the menu reset only runs when the task changes (task_panel.rs:923-927), reopening the same task may show the menu already open.
findings.principle: Esc cancels transient UI and doesn't navigate [MS-KBD]; users need a clear way out [NNG-H3]; same behaviour for the same kind of thing [NNG-H4]
findings.fix: Extend escape() to close the top overlay first and return true: if term_menu is set, clear it; else if att_drop is set, clear it; else take rev_pop. Clear all three in close_panel as well.

findings.title: Open-ended question has no answer here, only a quiet link that does three different things
findings.element: Task panel › banner › Write an answer, question state, all sizes and themes (question-open__light__1360x860.png)
findings.problem: The banner's only action is a borderless orange link, so the state that most needs a next step has the weakest control on the panel. It is also the only route: the banner holds no field, although the PR banner has one. The same label runs a different action by state (view.rs:1595-1600): it focuses the live terminal, reopens a terminal that asks again, or starts a fresh terminal from the handoff. The owner can't tell which will happen, and the ↗ icon suggests a web link.
findings.principle: Walkthrough Q2 and Q3 (notice the action, associate it with the result) [NNG-CW]; one primary action per screen [NNG-H8]; label says what it does [NNG-H2]
findings.fix: In view.rs:1600, when the question has no options, use Look::Primary instead of Look::Out. Name it by what it does: 'Answer in Midna' for focus, 'Reopen to answer' for a question with no live terminal, 'Resume in a new terminal' for the fresh case. Keep the quiet look only as the secondary route under one-click options, worded 'Write a different answer'. Better still, reuse answer_field and answer_btns (view.rs:1010, view.rs:912) so the open-ended question matches the PR banner: needs the owner's OK if a typed answer counts as outside the one-click rule, though the PR banner already does this.

findings.title: Looks finished recommends Resume, is alarm red, and its Mark done doesn't mark it done
findings.element: Task panel › banner › Looks finished (lost-looks-finished__light__1360x860.png)
findings.problem: The banner shows evidence the work shipped ('Opened a PR · 8:40 AM'), yet the blue primary is still 'Resume in a new terminal' and 'Mark done' is a plain button on a second row. Following the emphasis restarts finished work. The state is the good outcome but uses the same red as Terminal lost (view.rs:1551). 'Mark done' sends resume mode finish, which opens a new terminal to check the work and run tb submit (view.rs:1545-1546), so the label promises an instant result it doesn't deliver.
findings.principle: Walkthrough Q3 [NNG-CW]; match with the real world [NNG-H2]; one emphasis on the likely action [SEC-5]
findings.fix: When looks_finished is non-empty, make the finish action Look::Primary and first in the row, and Resume Look::Plain. Rename it 'Check and finish' on all lost forms, since a terminal does that work. Use a non-alarm tone for this form: BoxTone::Quiet, or a new tone on up_soft (#e3f4ea light, #16301f dark).

findings.title: Lost banners don't say what happened or when, and the timeline adds an empty Waiting on you
findings.element: Task panel › banner body and timeline bubble, Terminal lost, Stopped, Looks finished, Couldn't start, Couldn't compact (lost-terminal, lost-stopped, lost-looks-finished, start-failed, compact-failed captures)
findings.problem: Under five different headings the body is the same sentence, 'Wiring the assertion check into the session middleware.', the agent's last progress line. It reads as current activity, not as what went wrong. The helpful line 'The terminal closed before the task was done.' only appears when latest is empty (view.rs:1525), so it is hidden in the common case. No time is given, while may-be-stuck does give one. Stopped doesn't say that the owner closed it, which is the only real difference from Terminal lost apart from the tint. The timeline bubble below reads just 'Waiting on you', with no data, against the owner's no-filler rule. The start and compact bodies depend on whether the server rewrites latest on failure, which the excerpts don't show.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; recognise and diagnose errors [NNG-H9]; walkthrough Q1 [NNG-CW]; owner's rule: no labels that show no data
findings.fix: Lead with a state sentence and a time, then show latest as context in St::Small. Terminal lost: 'The terminal closed at 8:41 AM before the task was done.' Stopped: 'You closed its terminal at 8:41 AM.' Looks finished: 'The terminal closed at 8:41 AM, but its work shipped:' followed by the evidence lines. Second line: 'Last update: Wiring the assertion check…'. This needs a closed-at time on the task, in 12-hour form through fmt::hhmm. For the two failure banners, show the failure reason, not the progress line. Drop the bare timeline bubble when a banner already covers the state, or give it the same time.

findings.title: May be stuck has no action
findings.element: Task panel › banner › may be stuck, light and dark (stuck__light__1360x860.png, stuck__dark__1360x860.png)
findings.problem: This is the only warning banner with no button: it says something is wrong and shows the terminal's last lines, then stops (view.rs:1604-1609). The owner has to work out what to do. With a live terminal, Focus in Midna sits in the timeline's actions (view.rs:1647-1649), well away from the warning, and Close terminal is behind a ⋯ menu. The capture shows neither.
findings.principle: Walkthrough Q2 [NNG-CW]; no dead ends [NNG-H3]; frequent in view [SEC-8]
findings.fix: Add a row after the tail fold, using the group note as the other banners do: 'Focus in Midna' as Look::Primary (Act focus) and 'Close terminal' as Look::Plain (Act close-term, same force rule as view.rs:1655), with c.note(&grp). Stop is one of the allowed signals, so no rule changes. Show the row only when session_live(t); otherwise offer 'Resume in a new terminal'.

findings.title: PR banner and timeline contradict each other and offer competing next steps
findings.element: Task panel › banner › terminal asks about the PR, with the Checks and review section below it (pr-stopped__light__1360x860.png)
findings.problem: The banner says 'The fix agent stopped', while the row just below says 'Fixing the merge conflict' as if it were still running. The heading calls it asking, but the message states a stop and asks nothing. The owner sees six possible moves at once: Send answer, Focus in Midna, Terminal ›, Mark reviewed ›, Merge now ›, plus a second 'Waiting on you' cut off by the footer. Focus in Midna and Terminal › lead to the same place. Merge now stays on offer while the branch has a conflict. 'Waiting on you' appears twice, plus 'Waiting 12h 25m' on the reviewer. The heading's fallback 'Its terminal' (view.rs:1612) also names nothing useful.
findings.principle: One fact, one place [SEC-7]; one emphasis [SEC-5]; visibility of status [NNG-H1]; a primary surface with contradictory readouts is 3 Major [severity guide]
findings.fix: Make the banner the single call to action while pr_stopped is set. Change the stage row to 'Fix stopped' with the same tone as the banner and remove its Terminal › link, since the banner has Focus in Midna. Hide Merge now while the conflict is unresolved. Drop the lower Waiting on you bubble in this state. Word the heading by the message: 'Stopped on the PR' unless the message really asks something, and use the stage name instead of 'Its terminal'.

findings.title: Primary button text falls under AA in dark mode
findings.element: Task panel › banner › every Look::Primary button in dark, such as Resume in a new terminal (lost-terminal__dark__1360x860.png)
findings.problem: White on the dark accent_btn #4d72f0 computes to 4.22:1, under the 4.5:1 needed for text this size, and it is the main action on every banner. Light mode passes at 5.11:1. It is Likely because the button code isn't in the excerpts; the pairing is read from the token names (theme.rs:144, theme.rs:169) and the capture.
findings.principle: Contrast minimum [WCAG 1.4.3]
findings.fix: Set dark accent_btn in theme.rs:144 to #3563e9, the light value, which gives 5.11:1 with white. Check it still stands out on down_soft #3b1a19 and warn_soft #3a2415.

findings.title: Step row runs off the panel when a project has merge steps
findings.element: Task panel › Checks and review › step row, with merge steps. pr-merge-steps__light__1360x860.png and pr-merge-steps__light__900x560.png. Measured from the captures, the panel is about 480px wide at 900, 1360 and 1728, so a wider window doesn't help.
findings.problem: With six steps, the last one is cut at the panel edge and reads 'Merg' / 'To d'. A seventh step (the author-side review step, or another merge step) would be fully out of view. Nothing shows that more steps exist, and the code adds no wrap or scroll. Those are the steps that hold the PR back, so the owner can't see what it still needs. Cause: steps are flex_none (task_panel.rs:2013), and the row has no wrap or overflow handling (task_panel.rs:1596), with connectors keeping a 14px minimum (task_panel.rs:1599).
findings.principle: Every control at every size: nothing is lost at a supported width [NNG-H6]; narrowing keeps sections recognisable [SCR-6]; visibility of system status [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: When there are more than 4 steps, render them as a vertical list in c_steps: one row of about 28px per step, with a 16px dot, the name on the left and the state words on the right. As a lighter option, collapse finished steps into one 'Checks, You, Review done' stop and draw only the open steps in the horizontal row. Keep the current horizontal row for 4 steps or fewer.

findings.title: Orange 'needs you' also marks work that isn't the owner's
findings.element: Task panel › step row and reviewer rows. Review step in pr-changes-asked__light__1360x860.png and pr-long__light__1360x860.png; merge steps in pr-merge-steps__light__1360x860.png; reviewer pill in pr-rereview__light__1360x860.png.
findings.problem: Flow 4 depends on knowing what waits on whom, but the Ask look is used for three different situations. (1) Review shows orange '3 new comments' while the row below says an agent is already 'Answering 3 review comments' (view.rs:1920). (2) Every unfinished merge step shows orange 'To do' with a speech-bubble icon, but the panel offers no control for it and doesn't say who does it (view.rs:1944). (3) 'Re-review waiting' is an orange outlined pill although it waits on Dana, not the owner (view.rs:2021). The same state also has three wordings in one view: 'Awaiting re-review', 'Re-review waiting' and 'Re-review queued'. The owner has to read every row to work out which orange is theirs.
findings.principle: Consistency: one meaning per look [NNG-H4]; at most one strong emphasis, selected states quiet [SEC-5]; one fact in one place [SEC-7]
findings.fix: Keep StepSt::Ask and orange only for steps the owner must act on. When a live stage session is on the comments, draw Review as StepSt::Now with the same '3 new comments' link. Draw merge steps as StepSt::Wait, or Now for the running one, with words that name the actor, such as 'Agent next'. Keep Ask only if the owner runs that step, and then add the way to do it. Make the re-review pill Tone::Queued, and use one wording throughout: 'Re-review waiting' on the pill, plus 'Queued' as the note.

findings.title: Checks and review has no single next action
findings.element: Task panel › Checks and review, whole section. pr-changes-asked__light__1360x860.png, pr-long__light__1360x860.png and pr-stopped__light__1360x860.png.
findings.problem: The primary task is to do the one thing that moves the PR on, but nothing is emphasised as that one thing. These checks fail together. (a) One emphasis: Mark reviewed, Terminal, Merge now, Passed and '3 new comments' are all small blue links, and the owner's action sits at the right end of a grey row with the same weight as the agent's row above it. (b) One look per role: links come in four looks: underlined, underlined with a chevron, bold with no underline ('Terminal ›'), and the bold #944 with a separate external-link icon. State words change colour by whether they link, not by state: Done reads blue 'Passed' beside green 'Reviewed', and a failed Checks step reads blue 'Being fixed' under a red name (view.rs:1871). (c) Order: the owner's row comes below the agent's row, under the reviewer rows, so what needs the owner is the last thing read. In pr-changes-asked the section stacks 7 rows before the next stop.
findings.principle: One emphasis [SEC-5]; one look per role [SEC-4]; frequent in view [SEC-8]; aesthetic and minimalist design [NNG-H8]
findings.fix: Directly under the step row, put the owner's row first. When the You step is 'waiting', draw Mark reviewed as a soft button (Look::SoftSmall already exists) and keep it a link in the 'early' state. Follow with the agent's stage row, then the reviewer rows. Use one link look for every 'x ›' command by giving Terminal › the same look as Mark reviewed ›. Colour a step's link with the step's state colour, keeping the underline as the link cue.

findings.title: Merge now shows when it can't work or is already happening
findings.element: Task panel › Merge now. pr-stacked__light__1360x860.png, pr-stopped__light__1360x860.png (branch has a conflict), and phase 'merge' from code.
findings.problem: The code comment says only conflicts and the stack's order still stop a merge, but the condition checks neither (view.rs:2385). So it's offered on a stacked PR, next to 'Waits for #940 to merge into this one first', and on a branch with an unresolved conflict. Because Merging is StepSt::Now, the guard also leaves it visible while the merge is running. In the failed-checks state it reads the same as in a clean state, and that it bypasses checks and reviews appears only in a hover tooltip. I didn't see the confirm step or what a failed attempt shows. The control also sits under Checks and review, while the Pending merge stop stays empty.
findings.principle: Error prevention: constraints rather than error messages [NNG-H5]; visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; match the action to its result [NNG-CW]
findings.fix: Hide Merge now in phase 'merge', and in phase 'stack' and on a conflict, where the existing line already gives the reason. Move it into the Pending merge stop's body. Make the label name what it skips: 'Merge past failed checks ›', 'Merge without review ›', and plain 'Merge now ›' only when nothing is skipped.

findings.title: Step state text and the not-started ring fail contrast
findings.element: Task panel › step row. 'After checks' in pr-checks-running__light__1360x860.png and pr-checks-failed__light__1360x860.png; 'Reviewed' in pr-rereview__light__1360x860.png; empty ring on You. Dark for 'After checks' and the ring from theme values.
findings.problem: Computed from theme.rs against the card colour. The Todo sub-label (t.faint) is 3.04:1 in light and 3.80:1 in dark, which fails 4.5:1 at this small size. The Done sub-label (t.up) is 4.38:1 in light, which fails narrowly. It also applies to merge steps' 'Passed' and 'Skipped: why'. The Todo ring (t.border_2) is 1.48:1 in light and 1.63:1 in dark, under 3:1. A You or merge step with no words has only that ring to show its state.

findings.title: Reviewing means going below the actions to find the PR link

findings.title: The banner sends the owner to Midna for a task that has no terminal
findings.element: Task panel › banner above Yours to do, state to-do, all sizes and both themes (human-to-do__light__1360x860.png, human-to-do__dark__1360x860.png, human-to-do__light__900x560.png, human-to-do__light__1728x1084.png)

findings.title: The note field has no name, though the steps and Done depend on it
findings.element: Task panel › Yours to do › note field, states to-do and waiting, all sizes (human-to-do__light__1360x860.png, human-waiting__light__1360x860.png)
findings.problem: Step 4 says "in the note", but nothing on screen is called a note. The field is an empty box with placeholder "" (view.rs:1058). findings.principle: Visible labels or instructions [WCAG 3.3.2]; name, role, value [WCAG 4.1.2]; recognition rather than recall [NNG-H6]
findings.fix: Add a visible label above the field, "Note for the agents", in St::Small, and pass the same string as the field's accessible name. A placeholder would not do, because it disappears while typing. The field's placeholder was left blank, which looks tied to the no-filler rule. findings.title: A blocked task looks and acts like one you can do now
findings.element: Task panel › Yours to do, state waiting, both themes (human-waiting__light__1360x860.png, human-waiting__dark__1360x860.png)
findings.problem: The only difference from the to-do state is one small line, "Starts once T5 Set up signing is done". findings.title: Done can't be taken back, and it goes through with an empty note
findings.element: Task panel › Yours to do › Done, then the Done by you box (human-to-do__light__1360x860.png, human-done__light__1360x860.png)
findings.problem: One click on Done posts /did with whatever is in the field, including nothing (task_panel.rs:572-588), and anything waiting goes on. The finished box then has no action at all (view.rs:1041-1046), so the owner can't correct or add to the note, or reopen the task. A slip on the primary button of the flow has no way back from this panel. blocked_row wasn't in the excerpts, but no such control shows in the captures.
findings.principle: User control and freedom [NNG-H3]; error prevention [NNG-H5]
findings.fix: Keep Done one click, as the owner's rules say, and don't add a confirm dialog. Add a quiet "Reopen" button (Look::Plain) to the Done by you box, wired to the existing requeue act (task_panel.rs:534) or a human-task equivalent, and let the note be edited there. This is a new human-task signal: needs the owner's OK. For the empty case, when the steps mention a note and the field is empty, have the first press show "Send with no note?" through c.note(&grp) and let a second press send it.

findings.title: Several colours on the primary box fall under AA

findings.title: Closing during busy doesn't stop the action and throws away its result
findings.element: Finish confirm › Close button and Esc, in the busy state (Marking done…, Cancelling…, Merging…), all sizes and themes
findings.problem: Close stays live and Esc still closes while the request runs, so it reads as backing out, but the request has already been sent and carries on. When it returns, the handler finds no Finish modal and returns early: no success toast, no failure note and no m.refresh. A merge past review can land, or fail, with no word to the owner. If a new Finish dialog for the same task is open by then, the old result closes it. Proven by code: close() at modals.rs:101-103 and on_escape at 139-143 ignore f.busy; the early return is at modals.rs:294, and the ref check at 295-297 passes for the same task. Not seen running.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status, and user control: a command must report its outcome, and an exit must not imply a cancel that didn't happen [NNG-H1] [NNG-H3]
findings.fix: Pick one of two. Simplest: while f.busy, make on_escape do nothing and draw Close with kit::disabled and no on_click, so the dialog stays until the answer arrives. Alternative: let it close, but move the toast and m.refresh(cx) ahead of the modal check at modals.rs:294, and show failures as an error toast naming the task ("Couldn't merge T2's PR: <reason>"). Either way, carry an id on the request so a late result can't close a newer dialog.

findings.title: The confirm repeats the title instead of showing what the action will do
findings.element: Finish confirm › body, Merge now most of all (merge-now-modal__light__1360x860.png, merge-now-modal__dark__1360x860.png); also finish-done and finish-cancel in both themes
findings.problem: All three forms show only the task title. Merge now is an override past whatever holds the PR (modals.rs:31, 288), and in the capture the panel says 'Waiting on you' and 'Waiting on your review', yet the dialog names neither the hold nor the PR's own title. It also uses the same layout as a routine confirm. Mark done and Cancel likewise skip Midna's approval (modals.rs:22) on a task whose agent is still Working in the capture, and the dialog doesn't say so. With many agents running, the owner confirms an irreversible step from a line that tells them nothing new.
findings.principle: Error prevention: a destructive confirm must state the specific consequence [NNG-H5] [NNG-H3]
findings.fix: Add one line of live data, not helper text, so it fits the owner's no-filler rule. Merge: the PR title, then the holds it skips, such as 'Add passkey sign-in to the account page' and 'Skips: your review' (the Checks and Review values the panel already has, listing only what is unmet). Done and Cancel: the current state, such as 'Working · 5m'. Put it under finish-name at modals.rs:259 in muted 12.5px, and omit the line when there's nothing to skip.

findings.title: Dialog boxes are cut 10% short and sit off-centre, clipping the note's last line
findings.element: kit::modal_box, all dialogs: Note for testers › text (note-modal__light__1360x860.png, note-modal__dark__1360x860.png) and Finish confirm › bottom padding (all finish captures)
findings.problem: The Note dialog ends mid-line through 'audit log lists each change with its time.' at about 245px tall in an 860px window, with no scrollbar, fade or padding to show there is more. It is the view you open to read the whole note, and it is the one thing it fails to show cleanly. Measured from the captures, the boxes are 414 and 601px wide, not the 440 and 640 coded: 94% of the width, as in max_w(0.94). The same happens to height. Bottom padding under the Finish button is about 6px, not the 20 coded (modals.rs:258), the box's centre sits about 3% of its width left of the window's and about 6% of its height above, and all three window sizes agree. That points to the percentages in kit.rs:232-233 resolving against #modal-body's content-sized box (modals.rs:132), not the window; that cause is inferred from the measurements. A long failure note makes the Finish box taller, so the clip can eat into the action button, since its body is flex_none with no scroller. Alerts and New idea share this shell.
findings.principle: Text must not be cut off or lost, and the system should show there is more [WCAG 1.4.4] [NNG-H1] [SCR-4]
findings.fix: Remove max_w(relative(0.94)) and max_h(relative(0.9)) from kit::modal_box (kit.rs:232-233). Set the limits once on #modal-body (modals.rs:132), which sits in the full-size scrim: max_w(relative(0.94)), max_h(relative(0.9)), and make the box a shrinking flex child with min_h_0. Then the note grows to about 774px at 860 tall before it scrolls, the Finish box keeps its 20px padding, and the box centres. Add a visible scrollbar to #note-all for notes that really do overflow, and make the Finish body scroll so the button can't be clipped.

findings.title: Dark theme's Mark done label fails AA contrast
findings.element: Finish confirm › Mark done, dark, 1360x860 (finish-done__dark__1360x860.png); every kit::btn_primary in dark

findings.title: The panel stays 480px at every window size and covers the page instead of sharing it
findings.element: Task panel › frame, 900x560 to 1728x1084
findings.problem: Measured from the captures, the panel is about 480 CSS px wide at all three sizes. At 1728x1084 there is plenty of empty page, yet log filters still wrap to two rows and the prompt in Context stays narrow. The panel also overlays rather than pushes: at 1360x860 it hides the fourth stat card completely and cuts the Agents waiting card, at 1728x1084 it cuts the Waiting on you card, and at 900x560 the heading is cut to `1 a` and the card text mid-word.

findings.fix: Set the panel width to clamp(480px, 36% of the window, 640px): 480 at 900 and 1360, about 620 at 1728. From 1200px wide up, reserve that width in the page layout so page content reflows beside the panel instead of under it. Below 1200 keep the overlay.

findings.title: A long title takes nearly half the window and squeezes the body
findings.element: Task panel › header › title: long-text__light__900x560.png, long-text__light__1360x860.png
findings.problem: The title has no line limit and sits outside the scrolling body. findings.title: The `2 of 4` chip is unlabelled, sits beside a different `1 of 4`, and looks like a button
findings.element: Task panel › header › chips, all sizes

The sidebar shows `1 of 4` for the same goal on the same screen, meaning tasks done. Two near-identical numbers with different meanings invite a wrong read of progress. Both chips are filled, rounded grey shapes that look like soft buttons; whether they are clickable couldn't be read, because head_chips wasn't supplied.

findings.fix: Change the chip text to `Task 2 of 4`. If the chips aren't clickable, draw them as plain t.muted text separated by ` · `, so that fill is kept for controls.

findings.title: Close has no name or tooltip
findings.element: Task panel › header › close icon button, all sizes
findings.problem: `close_btn` passes None for its tip (view.rs:665), while the back button beside it gets `Back to …`. With an empty label too, the control has no text name for assistive technology and no tooltip to show a shortcut. The remove icon in Details has the same gap (view.rs:2657).

findings.fix: Pass Some("Close") at view.rs:665, adding the shortcut to the text if Esc closes the panel, and Some("Remove this row") at view.rs:2657.

findings.title: Agent text in the Now card shows raw markdown
findings.element: Task panel › Timeline › Now node: long-text__light__900x560.png
findings.problem: The capture shows a literal `**What to test:**` at the top of the Working card, because `latest` is drawn as plain text (view.rs:1428), while the What to do tab renders notes through note_body. The same state at 1360x860 doesn't show that line, so the two captures may hold different text; the plain-text path is proven by the code.

findings.title: Timeline times carry no date
findings.element: Task panel › Timeline › Started row and its Changes row, all sizes
findings.problem: Started shows `7:31 PM` and Changes shows `last commit 6:25 PM`, both from fmt::hhmm (view.rs:1140, view.rs:1176-1182). Every example of hhmm in the code is a bare time, and the row has no tooltip, while log rows get a full-time tooltip (view.rs:2752). A task started yesterday or last week would read like today, which matters for someone checking in through the day. The 12-hour format itself follows the owner's rule. The body of fmt::hhmm wasn't supplied.
findings.principle: Accurate system status [NNG-H1]; information not hidden behind recall [NNG-H6].
findings.fix: When the time isn't today, prefix it: `Yesterday 7:31 PM` or `Tue 7:31 PM`, and give the Started time the same `fmt::full_time` tooltip the log uses.

findings.title: The Full log count fails contrast and isn't part of the tab
findings.element: Task panel › footer › `5` after Full log, every capture, both themes
findings.problem: The count is 13px t.faint (task_panel.rs:1983): #8a95a3 on #ffffff is 3.04:1, and #6f7a88 on #1a1f26 is 3.80:1, both under 4.5:1. It is also a separate text node beside the button (view.rs:896-898), so clicking the 5 does nothing and the tab's name doesn't include the count.

findings.fix: Use t.muted (5.43:1 light, 7.12:1 dark) and draw the count inside the Full log button, so that it's part of the label and hit area.

findings.title: `What to do` holds the agent's brief, not what the owner should do
findings.element: Task panel › footer › What to do tab and its body: what-to-do__light__1360x860.png
findings.problem: The owner's task is to see what the task needs from them, and this tab name promises exactly that. It actually shows the task's description (`Add the login ceremony and the button on the sign-in page.`), which is the instruction for the agent. What the owner must do appears elsewhere, in the banner. The label sends the owner to the wrong tab in the moment they most need the right one.

findings.fix: Rename the tab `Brief` at view.rs:891.

findings.title: Context contains edit controls the read-only rule doesn't allow
findings.element: Task panel › Context › Details rows and Bits row; shown only when the task has them
findings.problem: Details draws editable Name and Value fields with a delete icon (view.rs:2652-2659) and saves on Enter (task_panel.rs:2191-2196). Bits has a `Mark created` button (view.rs:2565). No capture reaches this state, so this comes from the code alone.

findings.title: Branch and commit facts come from different sources on two tabs
findings.element: Task panel › Timeline › Started expansion and Context › detail rows: started-expanded__light__1360x860.png, context__light__1360x860.png
findings.problem: Started's `last commit` falls back to the log (view.rs:1176-1179), but Context reads only `where.last_commit` (view.rs:2587), so a task can show a last commit in one place and no Last commit row in the other. Context in the capture says Branch `Not reported yet` and Files touched `None yet.` while the log lists three commits; that gap may come from the overlaid capture data, but the code difference is real.
findings.principle: One fact, one place; no copies that can disagree [SEC-7].
findings.fix: Compute the last commit once in a shared helper using the fallback at view.rs:1176-1179 and call it from both tabs. Better, drop Branch and Changes from one of the two places: keep them in Context and let the Started expansion hold only terminals.

findings.title: Seven log filters wrap to two rows at every size, and some can't find what they suggest
findings.element: Task panel › Full log › filter chips: full-log__light__900x560.png, full-log__light__1728x1084.png
findings.problem: The seven chips never fit the 480px panel, so they take two rows even at 1728x1084; at 900x560 that is about 70 CSS px of a 368px body. Questions, Found and Jira show with nothing behind them for this task. The names don't match the row tags: Commit rows are under Turns (view.rs:2677). Note rows belong to no filter (view.rs:2682), so the Note row in the capture disappears under every filter except All.

findings.title: The log's helper sentence breaks the no-filler rule
findings.element: Task panel › Full log › text under the rows: full-log__light__1360x860.png, full-log__dark__1360x860.png

findings.title: The log filter probably carries over to the next task
findings.element: Task panel › Full log › filters, when opening another task
findings.problem: The filter lives in shared UI state (`u.log_filter`, task_panel.rs:448), and the reset on a task change clears term_menu, tl_open and rev_pop but not the filter (task_panel.rs:923-927). A filter set on one task would then hide rows on the next, which could show `Nothing of this kind yet.` beside a Full log count of 5. Nothing was run, and a reset elsewhere isn't ruled out.

findings.fix: Add `u.log_filter = "all".into()` to the reset block at task_panel.rs:923-927.

findings.title: Attached dropdown stays open across tasks and after use
findings.element: Task panel › header › Attached dropdown
findings.problem: Changing task resets term_menu and rev_pop but not att_drop (task_panel.rs:923-927), so the next task with attachments opens with its dropdown already covering the timeline. Clicking a row opens the item and leaves the dropdown up (task_panel.rs:1559). The chip's action has no just-closed guard (task_panel.rs:613), though the other two overlays need one for their outside-click close. That suggests Attached has no outside-click close at all; this part is Likely, because its renderer isn't in the excerpts. In attached-open__light__1360x860.png it hides the You and Review steps, which are what the task needs.

findings.fix: Add u.att_drop = false to the reset at task_panel.rs:923-927. Give K::Drop the same on_mouse_down_out and 300ms just-closed guard as c_term_menu. Close it after a row opens its item.

findings.title: Dropdown is placed by a fixed offset, not by the chip
findings.element: Task panel › header › Attached chip and dropdown, when the chips wrap to two lines
findings.problem: The dropdown is pinned at right_0, top 34px of a wrapping chip row (task_panel.rs:1498).
