The chip is then covered, and it may be the only way to close the dropdown (see R41). Even on one row the dropdown lines up with neither chip edge: the left edges are about 26 image px apart in attached-open__light__1360x860.png. No capture shows a wrapped row.
findings.principle: The control and what it opens stay related and reachable [NNG-H3] [SCR-4]
findings.fix: Anchor the dropdown to the chip the way c_rev_name does: anchored() from the chip's bottom-left, 6px below it, with snap_to_window_with_margin(px(8.)).

findings.title: Task and goal attachments are mixed in one ungrouped list
findings.element: Task panel › Attached dropdown › rows
findings.problem: The list chains the task's attachments and the goal's into one run (view.rs:715), and a row's owner appears, when it's set, only in the caption under the title (view.rs:752-754). The owner can't tell what belongs to this task and what was inherited. attached-open__light__1360x860.png shows only Design, Evidence and Doc, with no owner on any row. This is the problem the owner already corrected in L1.
findings.principle: Put a group's label above its members and indent the members under it [LESSONS L1]; one section, members grouped by function [SEC-1]
findings.fix: Add a heading for each owner, 'T2 Sign in with a passkey' then 'G1 Sign-in with passkeys', at 12px muted, with rows indented 8px under it. Remove the ref from the row's meta line. Omit the headings when only one owner has attachments.

findings.title: Close terminal takes effect at once with no undo
findings.element: Task panel › Done or Failed step › ⋯ › Close terminal
findings.problem: One click posts close-terminal (task_panel.rs:565), with no confirm or undo. On a failed task, the terminal may be the best record of why it failed, and it sits one menu away from Try again. Merge in the same panel does ask first (task_panel.rs:537). The ⋯ menu is a deliberate guard (view.rs:1373-1374), which is why this rates 2. The same item on a running task sends force in one click (view.rs:1655-1656). What the backend keeps after closing isn't in the excerpts.
findings.principle: Destructive actions can be undone or ask to confirm [NNG-H3] [NNG-H5]
findings.fix: Needs the owner's OK, since it changes a one-click signal: route Close terminal through the Modal::finish confirm that Merge uses, at least on failed tasks and for force closes, with the wording 'Close terminal for T2?'. Without that OK, keep the one click and show the terminal's last output in the Failed step, so closing it loses nothing.

findings.title: Menu helper text repeats the label, and can be false
findings.element: Terminal menu › Close terminal › second line
findings.problem: 'Closes the terminal it ran in' (view.rs:1382) repeats the label and shows no data, which the owner's rule forbids; see terminal-menu__light__1360x860.png. In the same menu on a live task, 'Stops the command that is running' is always shown, even when the session is idle and no command is running (view.rs:1655-1656).
findings.principle: Owner's rule: no helper text that shows no data; every element earns its place [NNG-H8]; plain truthful status [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: Remove the line from view.rs:1382 and have c_menu_item skip the sub div when sub is empty (task_panel.rs:1967). If a second line stays, make it data, such as 'Idle 12m'. At view.rs:1656 show 'Stops the command that is running' only when arg is force.

findings.title: Empty reviewer popover says the same thing twice
findings.element: Reviewer popover › head and body, with no open asks
findings.problem: The head says '0 open' and the body says 'No open reviews' (view.rs:2069, 2078), so a 480px card spends its whole body on a fact already stated. See reviewer-popover__light__1360x860.png.
findings.principle: One fact, one place [SEC-7]; owner's rule against filler; minimalist design [NNG-H8]
findings.fix: When open is empty, don't push 'No open reviews', and drop the head's bottom border when no list follows. The card then collapses to the name and '0 open', plus 'Reviewed this week' when there is any.

findings.title: Reviewer names don't look clickable until hovered
findings.element: Checks and review › Reviewers rows › name
findings.problem: At rest a name is plain text. The underline appears only on hover (task_panel.rs:1816), while nearby links such as Passed, 3 new comments and Merge now are underlined at rest. In reviewer-popover__light__1360x860.png, Dana Reyes and Lee Park read as labels, so the popover is easy to miss.
findings.principle: Will users notice the action is available? [NNG-CW]; links look like links [NNG-H4]; recognition over recall [NNG-H6]
findings.fix: Give the name a persistent 1px underline in t.border_2 at rest, turning to t.text on hover, or set the name in t.accent_fg to match the panel's other links.

findings.title: Reviewer popover doesn't fit the smallest window
findings.element: Reviewer popover at 900x560
findings.problem: The ask list has a fixed max height of 520px under a head of about 75px (task_panel.rs:1835), about 595px in all, in a 560px window with 8px margins. The last rows of a busy reviewer's list would end up out of reach. The card is 480px wide and sits left of the name. If the panel stays 480px wide at 900 (not confirmed), the name is near x=476, so the 8px snap slides the card right over the name it came from (task_panel.rs:1821). No capture exists at this size.
findings.principle: The layout reflows across the whole window range [HIG-MACOS]; focus and content are not obscured [WCAG 2.4.11]
findings.fix: Set the list's max height from the window: min(520, viewport height - 16 - head height). Below about 1000px wide, drop the card's width to min(480, name x - 26), or open it below the name instead of beside it.

findings.title: Reviewer and attachment lists aren't virtualized
findings.element: Reviewer popover › ask list; Attached dropdown › list
findings.problem: rev-list is a plain scrolling div that builds every open ask and every review from this week (task_panel.rs:1835-1842), which breaks the owner's rule. Attached builds a row for every task and goal attachment with no cap (view.rs:715, 719). Whether the dropdown scrolls or has a max height isn't known, as its renderer isn't in the excerpts.
findings.principle: Owner's rule: long lists virtualized; a list stays usable at many items [pass 7, data states]
findings.fix: Render both with the virtualized list the task log already uses (sync_log_list). Give the dropdown a max height of min(360, window height - its top - 8) with its own scroller.

findings.title: Reviewer popover has no retry and no refresh cue
findings.element: Reviewer popover › error state and reopening
findings.problem: A failed fetch shows 'Couldn't load their reviews: {e}' with the raw backend message and nothing to press (view.rs:2066). The only retry is to close and reopen. Each reopen refetches (task_panel.rs:556-558), but 'Loading…' shows only when nothing is cached (view.rs:2065), so old asks or the old error sit there with no sign of a refresh. Counts can be stale for a moment and look current. No capture shows these states.
findings.principle: Errors say what happened and what to do [NNG-H9]; system status is visible [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: Use 'Couldn't load Sam's reviews. Check that the board is running.', keep the raw text in the log, and add a Try again link that calls load_rev_asks. While refetching over cached data, show 'Updating…' at the end of the counts line.

findings.title: Hover feedback in the menu is almost invisible, and misleads on some rows
findings.element: Terminal menu items; Attached rows
findings.problem: Menu items hover to t.tint on a t.panel_2 card (task_panel.rs:1785, 1965), which computes to 1.08:1 in light and 1.17:1 in dark, so the destructive item barely responds to the pointer. Attachment rows use the same tint (task_panel.rs:1543); the dropdown's background isn't in the excerpts, though it looks the same in the captures. The tint also applies to rows with no link, which can't be clicked, because only the cursor and click depend on href (task_panel.rs:1557-1560).
findings.principle: Hover and pressed states are designed and visible [NNG-H1]; looks like what it is [SEC-4]
findings.fix: Add a menu_hover token, about #dde2e8 light and #343c47 dark, for roughly 1.2:1 against the card, and switch the sub line to t.text_2 on hover so it stays above 4.5:1. Apply the row hover only when href is Some.

findings.title: Lost banner's action row wraps, with a dead button taking the space
findings.element: Task panel › banner › action row, all lost forms, at 1360x860 and 900x560 (lost-terminal__light__900x560.png)
findings.problem: The panel stays about 480 wide at every window size, so three buttons never fit and Mark done always drops to its own row. The space goes to 'Reopen the old conversation', which is disabled when nothing was saved, with its reason only in a hover tip (view.rs:1538-1544). A control that can't work for this task pushes a real option out of line, and the banner ends up as four stacked rows.
findings.principle: Everything earns its place [SCR-5]; frequent in view, rare behind [SEC-8]
findings.fix: Leave out the Reopen button when claude_session_id is missing, instead of disabling it, so the two remaining buttons sit on one row. When it does exist, shorten it to 'Reopen conversation' and 'Resume in a new terminal' stays, with the finish action moved first or last per R8, and check the widths at 480.

findings.title: The same action has different names across banners
findings.element: Task panel › banner buttons, lost, compact-failed, start-failed and question states
findings.problem: Resume mode fresh is 'Resume in a new terminal' (view.rs:1537), 'Start fresh with the handoff' (view.rs:1575) and 'Write an answer' (view.rs:1598). Start mode new is 'New Midna terminal' (view.rs:1554) and 'Try again now' (view.rs:1565). The answer button is 'Send' in one banner and 'Send answer' in another (view.rs:972, view.rs:915). The owner has to relearn the same recovery in each state.
findings.principle: Consistency and standards [NNG-H4]; consistent labels [SEC-6]
findings.fix: Use one name per action: 'Resume in a new terminal' for resume fresh everywhere, 'Try again' for both start-failed variants with 'Queue in Midna' kept as the alternative, and 'Send answer' for both answer buttons.

findings.title: Option buttons look identical whether they send, pick one or pick many
findings.element: Task panel › banner › options, question-options and question-multi states (question-multi__light__1360x860.png)
findings.problem: All options use Look::Opt (view.rs:949, view.rs:951, view.rs:954). In one banner a click sends the answer at once. In another it only selects, and nothing shows whether a question takes one choice or several, though toggle_pick treats them differently. So 'Which sign-in methods stay on?' gives no clue that several can be chosen, and a click on a single-select question silently replaces the earlier choice. Send is greyed out with no sign of what's missing.
findings.principle: Looks like what it is [NNG-H4]; recognition over recall [NNG-H6]; error prevention [NNG-H5]
findings.fix: In select-then-Send banners, draw a leading indicator inside Look::Opt: a round radio mark for single-select and a square check for multi. Keep one-click options plain, so plain means it sends. This adds no helper text. When Send is disabled, name the question still unanswered in its tip, such as 'Answer “Where does the setting live?” first'.

findings.title: Answer field has no label, and empty Send only complains afterwards
findings.element: Task panel › banner › answer field and Send answer (pr-stopped__light__1360x860.png)
findings.problem: The field is created with an empty placeholder and no name (view.rs:1012), so nothing says what it's for, and Node::Field has no way to carry an accessible name. Send answer stays enabled when empty and only then says 'Write an answer first.' (task_panel.rs:478-481), while the picker's Send is disabled until ready (view.rs:972).
findings.principle: Labels or instructions [WCAG 3.3.2]; name, role, value [WCAG 4.1.2]; error prevention [NNG-H5]
findings.fix: Add a name to Node::Field and pass 'Your answer to <terminal>' as both the accessible name and the placeholder, so it carries real data. Disable Send answer and Send at … while the trimmed draft is empty, matching the picker, and keep the note as a fallback.

findings.title: Human-task question drops the result note and any alert
findings.element: Task panel › banner, question on a human task (not captured)
findings.problem: For a human task the banner returns early (view.rs:1590-1592), before c.note(&grp) and before the alert text is added (view.rs:1627-1629). An option click on a human task therefore has nowhere to show its sent or failed note, and an alert on that task never appears. It is Likely because the excerpts don't show whether human tasks carry ask options or how run reports failures.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; feedback after the action, walkthrough Q4 [NNG-CW]
findings.fix: Replace the early return with a branch that extends bx with c.note(&grp) and falls through to the alert code, returning the tone as (BoxTone::Ask, bx).

findings.title: Stage row says the agent is working after it stopped
findings.element: Task panel › stage row and banner, stopped. pr-stopped__light__1360x860.png.
findings.problem: The banner says the fix agent stopped, yet the row below still reads 'Fixing the merge conflict'. Only the dot and box colour change (view.rs:2355-2357), and the stopped wording is only in a hover tip. The banner's heading says the terminal 'asks' but the text is a statement. The owner also gets four prompts at once: the banner, the You step, 'Waiting on your review' and a 'Waiting on you' stop, with the review offered although the conflict is what blocks progress.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; one fact in one place [SEC-7]
findings.fix: When stage.stopped is set, change the row's words to 'Stopped: merge conflict not fixed', and keep Terminal ›. Keep the banner as the single call to action in this state, and drop the row's orange fill so the banner is the only strong emphasis.

findings.title: Pending merge's 'Waits on steps' hides who it waits on
findings.element: Task panel › Pending merge stop. pr-green-waiting__light__1360x860.png and __dark__.
findings.problem: This capture has no merge steps, and the only open step is You, yet the header says 'Waits on steps' (view.rs:1954). That's the board's internal phase word. The same wait appears three ways: 'Waits on steps', 'Waiting on you' and 'Waiting on your review'. Pending merge also gets a blue current dot directly above the orange one, so two stops look current.
findings.principle: Match between the system and the real world [NNG-H2]; one fact in one place [SEC-7]
findings.fix: Derive the sub-label from the first open step: 'Waits on you' when You is 'waiting', 'Waits on Rebase on main' when a merge step is first. Keep the Pending merge dot as StepSt::Wait with the plain hollow look, so only the stop that needs attention has a filled, haloed dot.

findings.title: Blocking PR #940 can't be opened from the panel
findings.element: Task panel › 'Waits for #940 to merge into this one first'. pr-stacked__light__1360x860.png.
findings.problem: The owner learns what blocks the merge but has to find #940 by hand, because waits_on_stack is drawn as plain text (view.rs:2348-2349). The sibling cases do link: 'Stacks on T3' and 'Waits on T3'. The fact is also split between 'Waits on stack' at the top and this line.
findings.principle: Recognition rather than recall [NNG-H6]; user control and freedom [NNG-H3]; consistency [NNG-H4]
findings.fix: Have the board send waits_on_stack as an object with ref, num, url and line. Render it like stacks_line: the task ref opens in this panel (Act 'open-task') and 'PR #940' opens on the host. Change the Pending merge sub-label to 'Waits on T7' to match the 'Waits on T3' pattern.

findings.title: Reviewer rows mislead on time and hide the popover
findings.element: Task panel › reviewer rows. pr-changes-asked__light__1360x860.png, pr-long__light__1360x860.png.
findings.problem: 'Changes asked · Asked 7:12 AM' reads as when the changes were asked, but it is when the reviewer was asked (view.rs:2038). On an approved row that time is no use, and on a Waiting row it repeats the pill. It also uses hhmm with no date, while the re-review branch uses day_time, so a wait of several days likely shows only a clock time. The name opens a useful popover of the reviewer's open asks, but it's a plain button with no tooltip and nothing marks it as clickable (view.rs:2010). Pills start at a different x on each row, and a long name drops 'Asked 7:12 AM' to its own line.
findings.principle: Match with the real world [NNG-H2]; recognition rather than recall [NNG-H6]; alignment [SCR-4]; no helper text that shows no data (owner's rule)
findings.fix: Show 'Asked …' only on Waiting rows, using day_time so it has a date once it's not today. Show the review's own time on Approved and Changes asked rows if the board has it, otherwise show nothing. Give the name a tip ('Their open reviews') and an underline on hover. Lay the rows out as a grid with a name column capped at about 150px, ellipsis on overflow and the full name in the tip.

findings.title: Merged-without-a-note state is a dead end
findings.element: Task panel › Merged › Note for testers, waiting. pr-merged-note-waiting__light__1360x860.png.
findings.problem: An orange 'Waiting' pill with 'Merged without one; the ticket waits' signals that something needs doing, but offers no action and no owner. 'One' makes the reader go back to the label to decode it. The same Needs tone is also used for 'Posting it, then moving the ticket', which needs nothing from the owner (view.rs:1707-1708).
findings.principle: Help users recover [NNG-H9]; no dead ends [NNG-H3]; plain language [NNG-H2]
findings.fix: Reword to 'No note yet, so the ticket stays where it is', and link to where the note gets written (Terminal › when a session exists). Use Tone::Queued for 'Posting it…' and keep Tone::Needs only when the owner can act. A one-click 'Write the note' signal would be cleaner, but it adds a signal to the read-only rule, so it needs the owner's OK.

findings.title: At the minimum window, Done and Talk it over are out of view
findings.element: Task panel › Yours to do, to-do, 900x560 (human-to-do__light__900x560.png)
findings.problem: At the smallest supported window the fold cuts through the note field, and Done and Talk it over aren't visible. The owner has to scroll to reach the one action the panel is for, and no scrollbar shows in the capture. The same thing will happen at any size once the steps are long enough, because the action row sits at the end of the content.
findings.principle: Walkthrough Q2, will users notice the action [NNG-CW]; frequent in view [SEC-8]
findings.fix: Removing the banner (R19, about 69pt) and the duplicate link button (R64, about 45pt) brings Done into view for this sample. For longer steps, pin the Done and Talk it over row to the bottom of the panel's scroll area, above the tab strip, so that it stays visible while the steps scroll.

findings.title: Numbered steps aren't a list
findings.element: Task panel › Yours to do › steps, all sizes (human-to-do__light__1360x860.png, human-to-do__light__900x560.png)
findings.problem: note_body only recognises -, * and • as list items (view.rs:2982), so "1. Open…" falls through to plain paragraph lines (view.rs:2987). Wrapped lines ("/api", "Manager.") return to the left edge under the numbers, and no gap separates the steps. Following a procedure while switching to another app means finding your place again, and the numbers don't stand out from the wrapped text. The structure isn't exposed either.
findings.principle: Info and relationships [WCAG 1.3.1]; visual hierarchy [NNG-VH]
findings.fix: Add an ordered-list branch to note_body that matches ^\d+[.)] and builds a K::MdOl, with the number in its own column of about 20px, a hanging indent for wrapped lines, and a 6px gap between steps.

findings.title: The link button repeats the inline link and can't tell two links apart
findings.element: Task panel › Yours to do › Open appstoreconnect.apple.com (human-to-do__light__1360x860.png)
findings.problem: The same URL appears as an underlined link in step 1 and again as a button, which costs about 45pt inside the box. link_label keeps only the host (view.rs:1027-1030), so two different pages on one host would give two identically labelled buttons, and the owner couldn't tell which is which without hovering. Whether the inline link is clickable isn't proven by the excerpts, since inline_text isn't among them; it is drawn as a link.
findings.principle: One fact, one place [SEC-7]; link purpose and consistency [NNG-H4]; every element earns its place [NNG-H8]
findings.fix: If inline URLs are clickable, drop the button row (view.rs:1053-1056) and shorten the inline text to the host plus the path, so the raw URL stops wrapping. If the button stays, show it only for URLs the step text doesn't already link, and label by host plus last path segment ("Open appstoreconnect.apple.com/…/api").

findings.title: The tab strip doesn't show where you are
findings.element: Task panel › footer tabs What to do, Context, Full log, all states (human-to-do__light__1360x860.png, human-done__light__1360x860.png)
findings.problem: In every capture none of the three tabs is marked, because the box is on a fourth view, TaskTab::Overview, that has no tab of its own (task_panel.rs:436-446). The owner can't tell what the current view is, or see an obvious way back to it after opening a tab. "What to do" also sits right under "Yours to do", so it reads as the same thing. The tab strip's code isn't in the excerpts, so the way back wasn't confirmed.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]; consistency and standards [NNG-H4]
findings.fix: Add a first tab, "Overview", and mark the selected tab with a bold label and a 2px accent bar. For a human task, the tab can be dropped while the box shows the steps, as long as the done state keeps them reachable (see R77).

findings.title: The two external actions look different, and the wrong one looks like a command
findings.element: Task panel › Yours to do › Open appstoreconnect.apple.com and Talk it over (human-to-do__light__1360x860.png, human-to-do__dark__1360x860.png)
findings.problem: Opening a web page is a bordered button with no icon, while Talk it over, a command that opens a terminal, is bare orange text with an external-link icon. Both leave the app, but only one says so, and the styling makes the link look like the action and the action look like a link. The orange is also the tone the app uses for alerts.
findings.principle: One look per role [SEC-4]; consistency and standards [NNG-H4]
findings.fix: Give Talk it over the bordered Look::Plain style beside Done, so the action row reads as buttons. Show the external-link icon on anything that leaves the app, or on neither. If R64 removes the link button, only the Talk it over change is needed.

findings.title: The dialog's action can't be reached from the keyboard in the code given
findings.element: Finish confirm › Mark done, Cancel task, Merge now, Close; Note for testers › Close and text scroller
findings.problem: Nothing in the supplied code gives the dialogs focus. Merge now and Show all open by setting m.modal and calling cx.notify (task_panel.rs:537-540 and 688-692), so focus doesn't move in. btn_base (kit.rs:129-149) has no focus handle or focus style, finish() binds only on_click, and #note-all can't take focus, so Tab, Return, Page Down and arrows have no target here. A person running this all day with hands on the keys has to reach for the mouse to confirm. The success path at modals.rs:300 also clears the modal without the window.focus call that the alerts path uses at line 111. Likely, because app.rs wasn't supplied and confirm_finish is pub, so a binding might exist there. Rated by the code seen: if none exists this is a 3 Major, as a WCAG failure on a primary flow.
findings.principle: All functions work from the keyboard, and focus moves into a dialog and returns to the opener [WCAG 2.1.1] [WCAG 2.4.3] [MS-KBD] [desktop:APG-DIALOG]
findings.fix: Give the modal a FocusHandle and focus it on open, through set_modal rather than a bare assignment. Bind Return to confirm_finish for Mark done only; leave Cancel task and Merge now off Return, so a stray keypress can't trigger them, and make them Tab-reachable with a 2px accent focus ring. Focus #note-all on open so arrows and Page Up/Down scroll it. Return focus to m.focus after success.

findings.title: A failed attempt removes the button, so there's no retry
findings.element: Finish confirm › failure state (finish-note), judged from code; not captured
findings.problem: Any failure sets f.note (modals.rs:308-311), and line 248 removes the button whenever a note exists. That is right for 'T2 is already done', but a dropped connection or board refusal gets the same treatment, so the owner has to Close and find the link again. The heading still asks 'Merge PR #944 now?' with nothing left to answer it, and the raw backend message is the only text.
findings.principle: Help users recover from errors; no dead ends [NNG-H9] [NNG-H3]
findings.fix: Separate the two kinds of note: keep already() results as final, and hold transport or refusal errors in a new field such as f.error. For f.error, keep the button and relabel it 'Try again', with the note above it. For final notes, change the title to the fact, such as 'T2 is already done', since there's no question left.

findings.title: A confirm opened from a terminal link can show only a ref
findings.element: Finish confirm › finish-name, when the task isn't the one in the panel; not captured
findings.problem: The title comes from the open task or task_card (modals.rs:230-231), and finish-name is simply left out when neither matches (line 259). A link for T6 opened while T2 is in the panel can read 'Cancel T6?' above a button, with T2's panel still visible behind it, so the owner may cancel the wrong agent's task. The already() check is also skipped until the panel has that task (line 232), so the button can show for a finished task; confirm_finish does recheck before acting. Whether the link path loads the task first isn't in the code given.
findings.principle: Recognition rather than recall: the confirm must identify its object [NNG-H6] [NNG-H5]
findings.fix: Fetch tasks/{ref} when the dialog opens. Until it returns, show the button as disabled with kit::disabled, then fill in the title and run already(). If the lookup fails, show 'Couldn't load T6' with no action.

findings.title: `3m · updated 3m ago` has an unlabelled number
findings.element: Task panel › Timeline › Now node sub-line, all sizes
findings.problem: The first `3m` has no label, so it isn't clear that it is run time (view.rs:1402). The equal values here come from the sample data, but the missing label doesn't.
findings.principle: The user's words [NNG-H2].
findings.fix: Write `Running 3m · updated 3m ago` at view.rs:1402.

findings.title: The least-used block on Context has the most emphasis
findings.element: Task panel › Context › What a new terminal gets: context__light__1360x860.png, context__light__900x560.png
findings.problem: The only tinted box and blue heading on the tab go to a long prompt the owner rarely needs. At 900x560 only about a line and a half of it shows, cut by the footer. The blue heading also doesn't match Files touched, which is the same level (view.rs:2665).
findings.principle: One emphasis, kept for what matters [SEC-5]; consistent labels [SEC-6].
findings.fix: Use the neutral box tone and t.muted heading, matching Files touched.

findings.title: Tooltip sits on the open menu, and open state is shown unevenly
findings.element: Done or Failed step › ⋯ button and terminal menu; Attached chip chevron
findings.problem: The 'Terminal actions' tooltip stays up after the click and overlaps the menu's top edge, in both terminal-menu captures. The ⋯ button shows no open state, while the Attached chip and reviewer name do. The Attached chevron points down whether open or closed (attached-chip__light__1360x860.png, attached-open__light__1360x860.png).
findings.principle: Selected and open states are designed [NNG-H1]; same thing, same look [NNG-H4]
findings.fix: Pass None as the tooltip while term_menu is set (view.rs:1380, 1651), give the ⋯ button the on-state look that Look::Chip uses, and flip the chevron up when att_drop is set.

findings.title: Stuck heading repeats the task title, in capitals
findings.element: Task panel › banner › may be stuck heading (stuck__light__1360x860.png)
findings.problem: 'T2 SIGN IN WITH A PASSKEY MAY BE STUCK' repeats the ref and title shown just above it, and a long title will wrap in capitals. The body also has a capital in mid-sentence: 'Since 8:20 AM: Its terminal hasn't moved on' (fmt.rs:209-211).
findings.principle: One fact, one place [SEC-7]
findings.fix: Use 'May be stuck' as the heading at view.rs:1605, and lower-case the default reason in fmt.rs:209 to 'its terminal hasn’t moved on'.

findings.title: Banner links sit 14px off the left edge, in two link styles, under a stray gap
findings.element: Task panel › banner › Write an answer, See what the new terminal gets, top edge (lost-looks-finished__light__1360x860.png)
findings.problem: These two links keep button padding and start right of every other banner row. In Looks finished, 'Opened a PR' and 'See what the new terminal gets' are both links but start on different edges. One link style is orange without an underline and the other blue with one. An empty white strip also sits between the header's divider and the banner's top border.
findings.principle: Alignment [SCR-4]; one look per role [SEC-4]
findings.fix: Remove the left padding from Look::Out and Look::Link inside a banner so they align with the text at the banner's 24px inset. Use one link style in banners. Remove the top gap so the banner's top border replaces the header divider.

findings.title: Note preview counts source lines, not visible lines
findings.element: Task panel › Merged › Note for testers. pr-merged__light__1360x860.png.
findings.problem: NOTE_PREVIEW_LINES is 3 source lines (view.rs:1721), so the capture shows 5 visible lines. A note written as one long paragraph would show in full with no Show all, pushing Checks and review down.
findings.principle: Aesthetic and minimalist design [NNG-H8]
findings.fix: Clamp the preview to 3 rendered lines, or cap it by characters at about 240, and show Show all when anything is cut.

findings.title: Merged stop doesn't say when
findings.element: Task panel › Merged stop. pr-merged__light__1360x860.png.
findings.problem: The Started stop has a time, but Merged has none, because its head's time slot is passed empty (view.rs:2411). An owner checking in through the day can't tell when it landed.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: Pass the merge time into tl_head's time slot, in the same 12-hour format as Started, if the board has it.

findings.title: The finished record has no time and no steps
findings.element: Task panel › Done by you (human-done__light__1360x860.png, human-done__dark__1360x860.png)
findings.problem: The box shows the note but not when it was finished, and the steps are gone from this view. Checking back later, the owner can't see when it happened or what was asked without going to another tab, assuming the What to do tab holds them.
findings.principle: Visibility of system status [NNG-H1]
findings.fix: Add the finish time in 12-hour form to the label ("Done by you · 3:12 PM"), and put the steps in a closed fold under the note, using the existing fold node.

findings.title: Header chips: alert tone on a finished task, and an unlabelled "2 of 4"
findings.element: Task panel › header chips, all states (human-done__light__1360x860.png, human-to-do__light__1360x860.png)
findings.problem: "Human task" keeps the warn colour even on a finished task, so a kind reads as an alert. "2 of 4" doesn't say what it counts, and this task happens to have 4 steps, while the sidebar's "1 of 4" for the same goal counts something else. The chip's code isn't in the excerpts, so its meaning is inferred.
findings.principle: Match with the real world [NNG-H2]; one emphasis [SEC-5]
findings.fix: Use the neutral chip style for Human task once it is done, or for every state. Label the position "Task 2 of 4".

findings.title: Busy button doesn't use the kit's disabled look
findings.element: Finish confirm › action button, busy state; not captured
findings.problem: Busy uses opacity(0.6) (modals.rs:241-245) while keeping the pointer cursor and hover fill, so it still looks clickable though no handler is attached. Its danger label drops to 3.08:1 in light and 2.91:1 in dark, which is exempt as disabled but is the only status on screen.
findings.principle: Disabled controls look disabled, and one look per role [NNG-H1] [SEC-4]
findings.fix: Use kit::disabled for the cursor, and drop the hover with a plain non-hover variant. Set opacity to about 0.7 so the 'Merging…' text stays readable.

findings.title: The way out sits apart from the action and isn't a clear 'no'
findings.element: Finish confirm › Close (24px, title row) and action button (30px, bottom right), all captures
findings.problem: A macOS confirm puts decline next to confirm. Here the decline is a small button in the heading row and the answer to 'Cancel T2?' is 'Close', so the pointer travels and the pair doesn't read as a choice. It is learnable, and avoiding 'Cancel' next to 'Cancel task' is sensible.
findings.principle: Platform convention for alert buttons [NNG-H4] [HIG-MACOS]
findings.fix: In the Finish form only, drop the head's Close and put a kit::btn labelled 'Keep task' (Cancel form) or 'Not now' (Done, Merge) left of the action in the bottom row, gap 8px.

what_works: Panel shell and tabs: The panel is one calm column with quiet chrome. The header, body and fixed footer read the same in all three sizes and both themes, and nothing overlaps or clips inside the panel at 900x560 with normal text.

Panel shell and tabs: The Now card is the one filled block on the Timeline, with a clear status pill and the agent's latest line, so it stands out once you reach it. The Started expansion opens in place and keeps its context.

Panel shell and tabs: Dark mode holds up: body text and muted text pass (muted is 7.12:1 on the card), borders survive, and no light colours are left behind. The only contrast failure found is the tab count, in both themes.

Panel shell and tabs: Times follow the 12-hour AM/PM rule throughout, log rows keep a full-time tooltip, and the log uses a virtualized list that fetches older pages, as the owner's rules ask. Group headings sit above their members (L1), and nothing here uses tabs for a growing set (L2).
Panel popovers: Text contrast passes on the overlays: muted on panel_2 is 4.84:1 light and 6.30:1 dark, and Close terminal red is 5.86:1 light and 5.13:1 dark.
Panel popovers: The reviewer name's open state (accent border and soft fill) ties the popover to its source, and the popover leaves the panel's rows readable beside it.
Panel popovers: Hover-card dates and reviewer times use 12-hour AM/PM, as the owner's rule asks.
Panel popovers: Terminal and reviewer overlays reset when the task changes, and their just-closed guards stop a toggle from reopening them on the same click.
Panel popovers: Close terminal is kept off the main row and marked in red, away from Try again; the ⋯ only appears when a live session exists.
Banners and answering: The banner is the first thing the eye reaches in every state, and its full-bleed band separates it cleanly from the timeline.
Banners and answering: One-click options with a short description beside each one make a decision fast, and fit the owner's one-click rule. Options sit under their question, as lesson L1 asks.
Banners and answering: Tone carries meaning: Stopped is quiet grey while Terminal lost is red, and each state also has a text heading, so colour isn't the only signal.

Banners and answering: Banners hold up at 900x560: the panel stays about 480 wide and nothing is clipped in the two captures. Times use the 12-hour format with AM/PM. Banner text on its tint computes above AA (8.46:1 light and 9.6:1 dark for warn_text, 5.6:1 and 5.46:1 for the red headings).
PR steps: The step row pairs colour with an icon and words, so state never depends on colour alone, and it holds up well in dark mode.
PR steps: The stage row with Terminal › ties an agent's work to where it's happening in one click.
PR steps: 'Pending merge' stays named for what hasn't happened yet, then becomes 'Merged' or 'Closed without merging', so the timeline never overclaims.

PR steps: Waiting pills show how long a reviewer has been waiting (for example 'Waiting 12h 23m'), which is what the owner needs when deciding whether to chase. Times follow the owner's 12-hour AM/PM rule.
Human box: One clear primary action: blue Done stands out on the warm box in both themes, and it is the only strongly emphasised control.
Human box: Drafts are safe: the note is kept in drafts and is only dropped after /did succeeds (task_panel.rs:570-576), so a failed send doesn't lose typed text.
Human box: The finished state is calm and honest: the box itself turns green and carries the owner's note, with no extra toast or filler.
Human box: The panel keeps a readable line length at 1728 wide and its layout doesn't stretch; one home for the task is respected, and the human-task actions stay one-click signals.
Finish and Note modals: Titles carry both the verb and the object ('Cancel T2?', 'Merge PR #944 now?'), and button labels repeat the verb, so the action reads without the surrounding context.
Finish and Note modals: 'Close' rather than 'Cancel' avoids a Cancel versus Cancel task collision, and the backdrop ignores clicks, so a stray click can't lose or fire anything.

Finish and Note modals: The re-check in confirm_finish looks the task up again before acting, so a task finished in the meantime gets a note rather than a double action, and the busy flag blocks double submits.

Finish and Note modals: Risk is well weighted: routine Mark done is filled, while Cancel and Merge use red outlined buttons. Body text is 16.17:1 in light and 13.61:1 in dark, the error note colour is 6.57:1 and 5.80:1, and the dialog holds at 900x560 with no overlap.
Finish and Note modals: No owner rule is broken: no filler text, nothing editable beyond the signals, and the dialogs stay within the right-panel model.
